newsitem.title: USA: HealthSouth acquiring Horizon/CMS for $900 million plus debt.
newsitem.headline: HealthSouth acquiring Horizon/CMS for $900 million plus debt.

text.p: In a deal combining the nation's largest network of rehabilitation facilities with the second-largest, HealthSouth Corp. said Tuesday it was acquiring Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp. for about $900 million in stock and the assumption of about $700 million in debt.
HealthSouth has become the nation's largest provider of outpatient healthcare services, mainly through acquisitions.
HealthSouth said that under the agreement, Horizon/CMS stockholders will receive 0.42169 share of HealthSouth for each share of Horizon they own.
Horizon's stock closed Friday at $14.25 on the New York Stock Exchange while HealthSouth closed at $43.125, also on the NYSE, which was closed Monday for the Presidents Day holiday.
Neither stock immediately started trading when the market opened Tuesday.
The combined entity will have one-quarter of the nation's outpatient rehabilitation centres and almost two-thirds of the 190 rehabilitation hospitals.
The acquisition of Horizon/CMS will also add 12 new markets in which the combined company can provide outpatient surgery and rehabilitation services.

"We are very excited to add the rehabilitation operations of Horizon/CMS, which ... (will) further enhance our ability to market our services to insurers, managed care plans and self-insured employers," HealthSouth Chairman Richard Scrushy said in a statement.

Horizon, based in Albuquerque, N.M., also owns, leases or manages 267 long-term care facilities, a contract therapy business holding 1,400 contracts, an institutional pharmacy business serving 38,500 beds, and other healthcare services.

However, the company also has had legal, financial and regulatory problems in recent years. Just last week it agreed to spend $20 million to settle a stockholders lawsuit alleging insider trading by some officials.
In December, Horizon paid $5.8 million to state and federal authorities to resolve allegations of billing fraud.
HealthSouth, which is based in Birmingham, Ala., said it expects the acquisition to add to earnings per share this year.
The deal requires approval from Horizon stockholders and clearance from antitrust regulators.
It also includes a $35 million break-up fee plus expenses of up to $5 million if Horizon/CMS ends the pact and is targeted for acquisition by another suitor, the companies said.
Neal Elliott, Horizon's chairman and chief executive, will join HealthSouth's board upon the merger's completion, which is expected this summer, the announcement said.
